response.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT k_symbol, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount FROM "order" WHERE amount > 2802 GROUP BY k_symbol), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS overall_avg FROM per) SELECT p.k_symbol, p.avg_amount, p.avg_amount - o.overall_avg AS excess FROM per p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_amount > o.overall_avg ORDER BY excess DESC;

assumptions.assumption: A large order is one with amount strictly greater than 2802; an order of exactly 2802 is not large.
The blank purpose code is stored as an empty string in k_symbol (the column is NOT NULL), so GROUP BY k_symbol makes it its own group with no special handling.
The overall figure is the unweighted mean of the per-purpose averages, not the mean over all large orders.

alternatives.interpretation: Large orders are those with amount at or above the cutoff (amount >= 2802).
